title: 10 Best Softr Alternatives for No-Code Apps in 2026 (Tested)
summary: Tested comparison of 10 Softr alternatives for data integrations, permissions, workflows, and total cost in 2026.
body_markdown:
**My shortlist starts with your app’s hardest requirement - not the lowest price.** I’d compare[Jet Admin](https://jetadmin.io/) for access controls,[Glide](https://www.glideapps.com/) for mobile-first tools, and[Noloco](https://guides.noloco.io/) or[Stacker](https://stacker.ai/) for client portals. For custom apps, I’d consider Bubble or[WeWeb](https://docs.weweb.io/) ; for developer-led internal tools,[Retool](https://docs.retool.com/) ,[Appsmith](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith) , or UI Bakery.[Airtable](https://www.airtable.com/) fits simple internal dashboards when your data already lives there.


Across these **10[Softr](https://www.youtube.com/softr) alternatives** , I compare data connections, permissions, design control, workflows, build effort, deployment, and total cost. *Some options require JavaScript* , so “no-code” doesn’t describe every tool here.


**Quick Comparison**


Platform Where I’d start Main trade-off


Jet Admin Database-backed tools with access controls Sales quote required; verify security features by plan


Glide Mobile-first apps Usage charges and user types affect cost


Bubble Custom SaaS products More setup and usage-based billing


Noloco Client portals with record-level rules Structured layouts and plan limits


Stacker Customer and partner portals Connections and pricing differ by version


WeWeb Custom front ends Separate backend and hosting costs


Retool Data-heavy internal tools JavaScript and developer time


Appsmith Self-hosted internal apps Coding needed for custom logic


UI Bakery Internal tools with self-hosting Check permissions and user billing


Airtable Internal dashboards and forms Limited layouts and paid editor seats


My advice: <u>test access rules and data writes before switching</u>, then price **12–18 months** of use. The pricing research is dated **September 26, 2026** , and was not independently verified on **October 23, 2026** - so I’d confirm current plans before buying.

The next sections examine setup speed, customization, permissions, and cost for each platform.


## 1.[Jet Admin](https://jetadmin.io/)


Jet Admin is best suited to internal tools with access controls and client portals that rely on direct database actions.


**Evidence note:** The supplied sources don’t fully verify CRUD or rollback behavior. Test both before using the app in production.


### Data Connections and Sync


The materials describe real-time reads and writes. Test create, read, update, and delete actions against your own data source, along with error handling and refresh behavior. Workflows and permission rules depend on how reliably that data stays in sync.


### App Design and Workflows


AI Builder turns prompts into a first draft - not a finished app. Documented features include multi-branch workflows, scheduled jobs, and approval steps. Jet Admin also lists server-side functions for secrets, external API calls, and business logic.


Version history is available, but **confirm what a restore includes** before relying on it. Once the workflow logic is ready, access controls need testing before launch.


### Permissions and Deployment


Jet Admin lists SSO, SAML, role-based access control, and audit logs. However, the supplied materials don’t fully document which plans include them. For client portals, test access using separate user accounts rather than relying on UI-only restrictions.


### Build Effort and Cost


The learning curve is low to medium, though granular UI controls take extra setup time. Pricing requires contacting sales. Ask for an itemized quote covering users, SSO/SAML, support, and infrastructure.


## 2.[Glide](https://www.glideapps.com/)


### Data Connections and Sync


Glide charges for updates tied to[Google Sheets](https://workspace.google.com/products/sheets/) and Airtable syncs, data changes, integrations, and API calls. **Update volume affects cost** , so estimate it before launch - especially if your app syncs often or relies on heavy automation.


### App Design and Workflows


Glide suits mobile-first apps, while Softr is a better fit for website-style portals. Glide’s computed columns and workflow builder let you add business logic beyond basic record actions. That flexibility still depends on how you divide access among user types.


### Permissions and Deployment


On some tiers, Glide charges different rates for business and personal users.


### Build Effort and Cost


The **Maker plan costs $60 per month** and includes unlimited personal users and 25,000 rows. The sources don’t specify included update credits or overage rates, so confirm both before buying.


## 3. Bubble


### Data Connections and Sync


Bubble connects to external sources through plugins or the API Connector, but **it doesn’t offer native sync** . You’ll still need to build workflows to keep external data in sync, so it’s a better fit if you can handle that work yourself. Its strength is complex app logic rather than fast, database-first portals.


### App Design and Workflows


Bubble’s visual canvas gives you more control over responsive pages than Softr’s prebuilt blocks. It also supports complex, multi-step workflows. The trade-off is setup time: **expect days to weeks** , not a quick build.


### Permissions and Deployment


For team builds, version control and editor seats affect how you work together and manage releases. Starter includes basic version control. Growth adds premium version control with up to 10 custom branches, while higher plans increase branch limits and editor seats.


### Build Effort and Cost


Watch **Workload Units (WU)** closely and cap overages before launch to keep usage-based costs in check. If you want simpler database-first app building, the next option takes a different approach.


## 4.[Noloco](https://guides.noloco.io/)


Noloco suits teams that need structured, database-backed client portals with tighter permissions than a basic portal builder offers.


### Data Connections and Sync


Noloco connects natively to Noloco Tables, Airtable,[SmartSuite](https://www.smartsuite.com/) ,[Xano](https://www.xano.com/) , and Google Sheets.[PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/) , MySQL, and[HubSpot](https://www.hubspot.com/) require Business or above. REST API integration is available only on Enterprise. Airtable schema changes may take time to appear in the app.


This setup helps teams build faster, but leaves less room to customize the design.


### App Design and Workflows


Noloco’s canvas is more structured than Softr’s block-based builder. Its built-in workflow engine supports multi-step professional services workflows, with **3,000 workflow runs on Pro** and **10,000 on Business** .


### Permissions and Deployment


Pro includes record- and field-level permissions, while Business adds unlimited user roles. Built-in multi-tenancy keeps each client limited to its own records.


You can use a custom domain on Pro. However, **Noloco is SaaS-only** : there’s no code export or self-hosting option.


### Build Effort and Cost


Starter is listed at $49 per month. Pro costs $149 per month with monthly billing and includes 10 team seats, 50 client seats, 50,000 rows, 25,000 synced rows, and 3,000 workflow runs. Check those limits against your portal’s user count, data volume, and automation needs.


Business is listed at around $319 per month, with 10,000 workflow runs, unlimited user roles, and priority sync. Extra team seats cost about $10 per month, and extra client seats cost about $1 per month. Whether those costs make sense depends on whether you need workflow automation or just a simple portal.


## 5.[Stacker](https://stacker.ai/)


### Data Connections and Sync


**Check the version first.** Classic supports Airtable and Google Sheets. Astra focuses on Salesforce and database connections and drops Airtable support. In Classic, portal users can view, edit, and submit records through forms that write back to the source. Users have reported real-time sync gaps, so test how soon changes appear before using it in production.


### App Design and Workflows


Stacker works well for branded customer or partner portals with filtered records and forms. It requires more manual page building than Softr’s blocks. The sources don’t confirm native approvals or automation caps, so check both before choosing it for workflow-heavy apps.


### Permissions and Deployment


**Granular permissions are a core strength** , especially when sharing existing Airtable records with external users through Classic. Test access with separate customer accounts. A filtered page alone doesn’t prove that users can’t access one another’s records.


### Build Effort and Cost


Keep Classic and Astra pricing separate. Classic reportedly costs **$9/month for 20 portal users** , with Pro at **$199/month** . The newer credit plan costs **$50/month for 250 credits** , or **$0.20 per credit** , and includes **$100 in trial credits** . Credit rules and internal-user pricing aren’t specified, so costs can climb fast for portals with external users and frequent updates.


The next option offers more front-end control, shifting the trade-off toward flexibility.


## 6.[WeWeb](https://docs.weweb.io/)


### Data Connections and Sync


**WeWeb builds the front end; you supply the backend.** It connects to Xano,[Supabase](https://supabase.com/) , and REST APIs, letting you use live data and build CRUD workflows for database-backed screens. You get more control, but your team takes on more work.


### App Design and Workflows


Responsive layouts, reusable components, and spacing controls offer more design flexibility than Softr’s prebuilt blocks, with less built-in structure. Visual workflows handle branching logic for complex interactions. **Expect more time spent building.**


### Permissions and Deployment


WeWeb supports Xano Auth, Supabase Auth, OAuth, and OpenID for authentication. **Enforce record access in the backend** , rather than relying on front-end restrictions, for stricter data control. You can deploy through WeWeb’s cloud or export your code, but either option still requires an external backend.


### Build Effort and Cost


Your costs cover the builder, hosting, and backend. Sources disagree on code-export pricing, so check export eligibility and self-hosting costs before you buy.


The next platform takes a different approach, with more of the backend included.


## 7.[Retool](https://docs.retool.com/)


Retool suits teams that need more control than a block builder offers.


### Data Connections and Sync


Retool connects to SQL databases, APIs, data warehouses, and GraphQL, making it a good fit for data-heavy internal apps. It works well for teams that want direct database control instead of a prebuilt portal structure. Before building, decide whether you need live reads, scheduled syncs, or write-back logic.


### App Design and Workflows


**Retool is low-code, not no-code.** Its canvas UI and JavaScript support multi-step forms, filters, and custom logic, but technical teams will get more out of these tools. Expect more development work than with Softr’s simpler block-based approach.


### Permissions and Deployment


Retool includes version control, audit logs, environments, and cloud or self-hosted deployment. Availability and limits vary by plan, so check which tier includes the controls you need.


### Build Effort and Cost


**Budget for developer time and backend setup - not just the subscription.** The supplied research lists pricing at about $30 per user per month, but pricing details for builders, users, AI, workflows, and self-hosting are incomplete. Confirm those costs before setting your budget. Developer time is the main additional cost driver.


## 8.[Appsmith](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith)


Appsmith suits teams that want more control than a block builder offers - and are willing to spend more time building to get that flexibility.


### Data Connections and Sync


Appsmith is an internal app builder for tools that need custom interactions with user data. The supplied research does not confirm which connectors it supports or how CRUD refreshes work.


### App Design and Workflows


The canvas includes **over 45 prebuilt widgets** , such as Tables, Charts, Forms, and Modals. Events like` onRowSelected` and` onClick` trigger actions, giving you finer control than Softr’s block-based system.


Appsmith is low-code, but you’ll need JavaScript for custom logic and data transformations.


### Permissions and Deployment


Appsmith supports Git workflows, audit logs, and **self-hosted or on-premises deployment** . Softr, by comparison, is SaaS-only.


### Build Effort and Cost


The supplied research includes no verified pricing, so leave Appsmith out of the pricing comparison table.


The next platform offers similar control with a stronger focus on UI, changing the trade-off again.


## 9. UI Bakery


### Data Connections and Sync


UI Bakery balances speed and control. It suits database-backed internal tools when you need self-hosting. The research doesn’t confirm connector coverage or CRUD reliability, so **test write-backs and check that changes persist after reloading** before launch.


### App Design and Workflows


UI Bakery is low-code, but custom logic requires JavaScript. That means more setup than Softr. The research doesn’t confirm SQL support, conditional visibility, or how much its workflows can handle.


### Permissions and Deployment


**Self-hosting is supported** , but the research doesn’t confirm cloud deployment, granular permissions, dev/prod separation, or audit logs by plan. These unknowns matter most for internal tools with strict governance requirements. If self-hosting and JavaScript work for your team, pricing is the next filter.


### Build Effort and Cost


The research lists a free plan and paid plans starting at **$20 per user per month** . It doesn’t verify whether developers and end users are charged separately, so total costs remain unclear. Next, the comparison moves to a more data-first option.


## 10.[Airtable](https://www.airtable.com/)


### Data Connections and Sync


Airtable Interfaces runs on an Airtable base. Data from other sources must first be imported or synced through integrations or APIs.


### App Design and Workflows


Airtable offers prebuilt blocks for dashboards and forms. Built-in automations handle task routing and alerts without external automation tools. **Layout control stops at Airtable’s blocks** - you don’t get a fully custom canvas. This simpler setup works best when access stays internal.


### Permissions and Deployment


Access follows collaborator permissions, and editors need paid seats. Airtable works well for internal tools, but external portals require another layer of permissions on top.


### Build Effort and Cost


The interface layer comes with paid Airtable plans, so you can build simple internal apps fast. But **per-user editor charges can increase costs as your team grows** . That trade-off matters most when comparing Airtable with more flexible app builders.

## Final Verdict: Choose for Your App, Team, and Budget


Use the comparison above to choose based on your data source, permissions, workflow needs, and budget - not a feature checklist. **Keep Softr only if your app is mostly for reading data, uses simple forms, and doesn’t need row-level rules or audit logs.**


For growing operations teams that have outgrown simple portals, **switch only when the replacement solves a confirmed problem** . That might mean removing reporting and filtering limits or working around Airtable’s row, record, or automation limits.


For security-conscious enterprises, treat **SSO, SAML, and audit trails as launch requirements** . Check that your chosen plan includes each one.


Before switching, spend **20–30 minutes** building a test version of your hardest screen, data connection, permission rule, and workflow. Test with both internal staff and external client roles, and verify that clients cannot access another client’s records. Choose only after the test passes and you’ve priced **12–18 months of ownership in USD** , including users, data volume, automation runs, security features, and migration labor.


## FAQs


### How can I migrate my app without downtime?


You can migrate **without downtime** by rebuilding the front end while keeping your existing database. Connect the new platform to your current Airtable, Google Sheets, or SQL data source. Your data stays where it is.


Start with one key workflow or user group. Check permissions and performance, then switch over in phases. Watch for data sync issues and train your internal teams to use the new platform.


### How do I test client data isolation?


**Test permissions yourself** instead of relying only on vendor descriptions. Connect your actual data source in a test environment with one internal staff member and two external client users.


Check that each client can view, edit, or access only their organization’s records. Confirm that **row-level permissions** keep clients from seeing each other’s data - even when submitting, reviewing, and approving requests.


### How can I estimate costs as my app grows?


**Estimate costs based on expected growth over the next 12 to 18 months** , not just today’s headcount. Review per-user and usage-based charges, whether internal and external seats have separate prices, and any limits on records or database actions.


Include higher-tier plans needed for must-have features, possible seat or data overage fees, and maintenance time. Usage-based charges, such as workload units or AI credits, can be harder to predict as traffic grows.
